KO.rationale: Coca-Cola is a high-quality defensive franchise with strong brand equity, global distribution, and an asset-light concentrate model that generates robust margins (28% operating margin, 25.9% net margin, 40.4% ROE). Q2 2025 showed solid sequential growth (+12.6% revenue QoQ, +14.3% EPS QoQ) and Q1 2026 results beat expectations with revenue of $12.47B (+11.2% YoY) and EPS of $0.86. The company holds ~46% global sparkling soft drink share and is a Dividend King with 64 consecutive years of dividend increases. However, the stock is trading near the top of its 365-day valuation range (P/E 28.7x vs. range 23.2-29.0x, P/B 11.6x vs. range 9.4-11.7x), leaving limited upside from multiple expansion. Rising 10-year Treasury yields (4.57%) and elevated oil prices ($100/bbl) create macro headwinds for a defensive name that typically competes with risk-free income. The balance sheet shows elevated liabilities ($74.15B vs. $30.18B equity) though cash is adequate at $12.25B. No clear near-term fundamental catalyst is visible beyond continued execution. The score reflects a solid but fully-priced franchise with limited rerating potential at current levels.
